title: Shaybanids
capsule: The Shaybanids were a Turko-Mongol dynasty descended from Shiban, grandson of Genghis Khan, who rose to regional dominance under Muhammad Shaybani Khan (r. 1500–1510), seizing Samarkand from the last Timurid ruler Babur in 1500 and consolidating the Uzbek khanate across Transoxiana. Shaybani's conquest ended a century and a half of Timurid cultural patronage, though his own court supported Persian literary culture. The dynasty's early phase closed abruptly when the Safavid Shah Ismail I defeated and killed Shaybani Khan at the Battle of Merv in 1510; Shaybanid successors retained Transoxiana and continued ruling in various configurations until the line ended in 1598.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The Shaybanid heartland in Transoxiana is well documented; the fluctuating steppe frontier to the north and the Khurasan boundary with the Safavids shifted repeatedly and is difficult to map precisely.
